title: Platform Systems & Services: Runbooks, Dashboards, and Roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document collects the canonical inventory, runbooks, dashboard and alerting standards, and short-term roadmap for Redwood Inference platform systems and services. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and on-call responders. The goal is to provide a single reference that reduces time-to-diagnose, clarifies ownership, and records planned improvements for Q2 2026.

Scope

- Systems covered: control plane services (platform-control-plane), agent fleet (platform-agent), telemetry pipeline (platform-telemetry), placement & scheduler (placement-scheduler), ingress/egress proxies (ingestion-proxy), and shared infra (kv-cache-service, redis-cache, postgres-meta).
- Not covered: customer private deployments (see eng-private-deployments), model-serving runtime internals (see eng-serving-runtime).

Service Inventory (summary)

1) platform-control-plane
   - Owner: Platform Core (team). Primary contact: asha.patel@redwood.ai
   - Purpose: API surface for routing requests, tenant config, rollouts, and auth.
   - SLA: 99.95% availability for control-plane API; p95 latency < 150ms for control-plane calls.

2) platform-agent
   - Owner: Platform Agents (team).
   - Purpose: lightweight processes that run on worker nodes to manage model containers, KV cache warmup, and health reporting.

3) platform-telemetry
   - Owner: Observability (team).
   - Purpose: receive metrics/traces/logs, forward to prometheus/loki/tempo, apply retention & cost controls.

4) placement-scheduler
   - Owner: Runtime Scheduling (team).
   - Purpose: allocate GPU pools, pack workloads, enforce reserved capacity.

Operational SLOs & Error Budget

- Global: 99.95% availability across critical control-plane endpoints (login, route-decision, placement-request).
- Latency: p95 request time <= 150ms for control-plane, <= 300ms for placement scheduling under normal load.
- Error budget burn policy: SRE oncall to open incident when 3 consecutive days of availability breach (or single-day > 2x allowed error budget).

Dashboards (standard panels and queries)

Refer to the standard Grafana folder: /dashboards/platform/critical-services. Panels below should exist for each service. Sample queries and panels: (Prometheus examples)

- Control-plane p95 latency (Histogram)
  PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="platform-control-plane"}[5m])) by (le))
  Panel: p95 latency (ms), moving 5m window.

- Error rate (5m)
  PromQL: sum(rate(platform_request_errors_total{job=~"platform-.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(platform_request_total{job=~"platform-.*"}[5m]))
  Panel: stacked by service; threshold line at 0.01 (1%).

- Agent heartbeat gap
  PromQL: max_over_time(time() - platform_agent_last_heartbeat_seconds{job="platform-agent"}[10m])
  Alert: > 120s for any agent -> paging.

- Scheduler pending queues
  PromQL: sum(platform_scheduler_pending_tasks_total) by (pool)

Alerting standards and example rules

Alerts are defined in the prometheus-alerts repo and must follow the policy below: severity: critical|warning; team:label; page_after: immediate for critical. All alerts must include runbook_url label. Example rule (YAML excerpt):

- alert: ControlPlaneHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(platform_request_errors_total{job="platform-control-plane"}[5m])) / sum(rate(platform_request_total{job="platform-control-plane"}[5m])) > 0.02
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: critical
    team: platform-core
  annotations:
    summary: "High error rate in platform-control-plane (>2%)"
    runbook: "https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-platform/platform-control-plane-runbook"

- alert: PlatformAgentHeartbeatMissing
  expr: (time() - platform_agent_last_heartbeat_seconds) > 120
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: critical
    team: platform-agents
  annotations:
    summary: "Agent heartbeat missing for >120s"
    runbook: "https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-platform/agent-operator-runbook"

Runbooks (incident playbooks)

Common incident triage steps (applies to most critical alerts):

1) Acknowledge and record
   - Oncall engineer acknowledges in PagerDuty and opens an incident in Incident Manager (link: /oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process).
   - Record start time and initial symptom.

2) Identify blast radius
   - Check dashboards: control-plane errors, placement pending, upstream dependencies (auth, postgres, redis).
   - Query: curl -s https://platform-api.internal/healthz | jq .status

3) Execute containment actions (examples)
   - If control-plane error-rate high and tracing shows DB is failing: fail open read-only mode via feature-flag endpoint: POST /admin/feature-flags/fail_open
   - If agent heartbeat missing across a region: trigger agent-restart job: kubectl -n platform rollout restart daemonset/platform-agent-<region>

4) Remediation
   - If DB connectivity: engage database-oncall (pg-sre) and restore connectivity; apply read-only migration to prevent data loss.
   - If scheduler overloaded: scale placement-scheduler horizontally (kubectl scale deployment/placement-scheduler --replicas=<n>).

5) Recovery verification
   - Verify p95 latency back under threshold for 15 minutes and error rate < 0.5% for 30 minutes before closing.

6) Post-incident tasks
   - File postmortem (90% latency/availability incident) referencing timeline, impact, root cause, detection gap, remediation steps, and follow-ups. Assign owners and target dates.

Operational runbook: Control-plane partial outage (TL;DR)

- Symptom: control-plane 5xx spike and p95 > 300ms.
- Immediate: set ingress-rate-limit to 50% via orchestration API to reduce load.
- Short-term: migrate traffic to warm standby region using routing policy (console: Routing -> Policies -> Failover -> Activate standby).
- Long-term: investigate hot paths (auth DB queries, heavy telemetry writes), add index / tune queries.

Dashboards ownership and runbook links

- platform-control-plane dashboard -> runbook URL: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-control-plane-runbook
- platform-agent dashboard -> runbook URL: /confluence/eng-platform/agent-operator-runbook
- placement-scheduler dashboard -> runbook URL: /confluence/eng-platform/placement-scheduler-runbook

Instrumentation checklist for new services

Every new platform service must include before production rollout:

- Metrics: request_total, request_errors_total, request_duration_seconds histogram, queue_depth, worker_count.
- Health: /healthz returning code and last_processed_timestamp.
- Traces: OpenTelemetry instrumentation with service.name and request.id propagation.
- Logs: structured JSON with level, service, trace_id, request_id.
- Dashboards: basic 4-panel dashboard auto-created by infra pipeline.
- Alerts: critical error-rate, heartbeat missing, p95 latency breach, sustained cpu > 85% for 10m.

Platform Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)

1) Unified Incident Automation
   - Deliver runbook-driven automation for common containment tasks (scale scheduler, restart agents, toggle fail-open) via Runbook Bot. Target: end of Q2. Owner: Platform Automation.

2) Dashboard quality audit and templating
   - Convert ad-hoc dashboards into standardized templates (panels, thresholds, annotations). Decrease mean time-to-detect (MTTD) target by 25% by Q3. Owner: Observability.

3) Cost-aware alerting
   - Add cost signals (egress, telemetry ingestion) into routing policies to reduce burst cost. Pilot: dedicated GPU pools. Owner: Platform Economics.

4) Agent resiliency improvements
   - Replace agent heartbeat with a push-based lease model; reduce false-positive pages by 90%. Owner: Platform Agents.

5) Oncall playbook refresh and game-day
   - Run 2 game-days against placement-scheduler failure modes; update runbooks. Owner: SRE.

Retrospective highlights (recent incidents)

- Incident: placement-scheduler overload (Dec 2025)
  - Root cause: unbounded retry loop in placement client, causing queue growth and CPU saturation.
  - Actions: introduce exponential backoff, rate-limit retries, and add queue-depth alert.
  - Status: deployed Jan 2026; follow-up: add pre-deploy load test for scheduler.

- Incident: high telemetry ingestion costs (Nov 2025)
  - Root cause: verbose debug logging enabled in prod for 3 services after a deploy.
  - Actions: rollback logging config, add deploy-time lint to prevent debug-level env in prod, add cost dashboard and alerting.

Onboarding & team wiki pointers

- How to add a dashboard: /confluence/eng-platform/howtos/add-dashboard
- Alert rule PR process: create PR in prometheus-alerts repo, include runbook, add reviewer from owning team.
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-platform/templates/runbook-template

Ownership and escalation

- Primary on-call groups: platform-core-oncall, platform-agents-oncall, observability-oncall, runtime-scheduler-oncall.
- PagerDuty escalation policy: 15m -> 30m -> leader. Critical pages must reach leader in 30 minutes.

Appendix: example queries, CLI snippets, and troubleshooting tips

- Quick health check: curl -s https://platform-api.internal/healthz | jq .
- Restart scheduler: kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/placement-scheduler
- Query recent 5xx errors: promql: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-control-plane",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
- How to reduce noise:
  1) Move noisy alerts to warning severity.
  2) Add labels to alerts to scope to environment (prod/staging) and region.

Change log

- 2025-10-15: initial draft.
- 2025-12-05: added scheduler incident retrospective and instrumentation checklist.

If you have corrections or missing ownerships please add comments on this page or open a PR against the templates repo.
